question: Can the wall time of the full 8937-bright-field fit - 200 TPE global trials plus Nelder-Mead refinement - be reduced on Apple M5 by (A) keeping the 9.41 GB blocked phase-loss intermediate on chip, or (B) evaluating several independent candidates per cached bright-field read, while preserving the frozen objective exactly?

entrypoints: experiments/20260916-metal-ssb-objective-profile/probe4.swift (multi-candidate parity/timing record, retained but not built)
code.temporary_instrumentation: All source changes used for these arms were reverted; the landed source is exactly 597b566. The instrumentation was: (1) the round-1 env gates SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_{COLUMN,ROWS,NYQUIST} and SSB_PHASE_BATCH, retained as profile-gates.patch; (2) three profiling-only kernels in Resources/ssb.metal with deliberately broken parity - ssb_correct_half_column_ifft512_hermitian_linear (coalesced-store ceiling), ssb_correct_half_column_ifft512_hermitian_nofft and ssb_ifft512_rows_hermitian_phase_moments_nofft (transform removed, global traffic unchanged); (3) MetalSSBEngine.phaseVarianceBatch plus the PhaseLossTargets/batchTargets plumbing and the SSB_MULTI_BATCH_PLANES per-candidate chunk knob; (4) MetalSSBOptimizer batchTrialLimit (SSB_BATCH_TRIALS) and the SSB_OPTIMIZE_BATCH wiring of evaluateBatch in MetalSSBEngine.optimize. The single-candidate path is byte-for-byte unaffected by all of (1)-(4), which is why the control arm reproduces the frozen loss.
code.note: The frozen reference is fit loss 0.1376979947090149 at 597b566. Every arm here re-derives it from the single-candidate path; only the batched arms differ.

parameters.scope: Fit wall time at the native 8937-BF full-disk objective on one machine. Not a frame-rate or application claim.

execution.gpu_model: Apple M5 10-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory
execution.contention_note: Every run was taken under the shared GPU lock. Host load is stated with every timing set because it moves the objective by ~10%: the same fit measures 61.97 s at load 1.86 and 67.99 s at load 3.28, and the loss p50 moves 279 ms (load 0.6-2.8) to 309 ms (load 2.3-2.6). The A/B arms were interleaved in balanced order (the arm that runs first alternates with the round and group index) so neither arm owns a fixed position. The probes record load_average from /proc/loadavg, which does not exist on macOS and reads back as n/a; the load averages quoted here were taken from uptime in the driving shell immediately before and after each run.

headline.change: none landed; both levers measured as regressions and were reverted
headline.load_average_note: This is the low-load headline. Host load average is stated with every timing set: fit 61.97 s at load 1.86, 67.99 s at load 3.28. Loss p50 279.0 ms at load 0.6-2.8, 309.0 ms at load 2.3-2.6.

lever_a_intermediate.verdict: not achievable on this hardware; the blocked intermediate is a full-plane transpose buffer that cannot fit on chip at any granularity
obstruction: maxThreadgroupMemoryLength is 32768 bytes on this device. One bright-field plane of the intermediate is 512 x 257 complex64 = 1052672 bytes, 32x the whole threadgroup memory budget.

The two passes are transposed relative to each other: every output row of the row pass needs all 257 columns of the intermediate, and the column pass produces one column at a time. A threadgroup can hold one input column (4 KB) or one 4-row output block (8.2 KB), but the producer data for a 4-row block is spread over all 257 column tasks.

No per-dispatch batch makes the round trip cache-resident. Round 1 measured loss p50 272.6/273.3/273.2/283.4 ms at 4/8/16/32 planes per dispatch, i.e. a 4.2 MB to 33.6 MB live intermediate, with the smallest footprint 1.1% slower than the default. If residency were reachable at any of those sizes, the 4.2 MB arm would have won.

The access pattern is not the cause either: the coalesced-store variant of the column pass measured 155.3 ms against 157.7 ms for the blocked 4-row store, so rewriting the output layout is neutral, and the column pass already runs at 138.8 GB/s of combined read+write against the ~139 GB/s mixed-stream ceiling measured on this device.

lever_b_batching.verdict: rejected; measured slower than the single-candidate path at every footprint, and it changes the search trajectory
lever_b_batching.predicted_but_refuted: Batching 2 should have amortized the 9.41 GB bright-field read to 0.86x and batching 4 to 0.785x if the shared chunk were served from cache. Measured 0.908x and 0.911x, i.e. 10% slower rather than 14-21% faster.

objective_exactness.method: all 200 K=4 trial points re-evaluated through the single-candidate path

trajectory.k2_shared_trial_points: 11 of 200, first divergence at trial index 11
trajectory.k4_shared_trial_points: 10 of 200, first divergence at trial index 10
trajectory.cause: SSBOptimizer.run draws each candidate from the trial history, and the history is appended only after the whole batch returns, so a batch of 2 or 4 draws every candidate from the same history snapshot. This is a behaviour change, not just a speed change.
trajectory.effect: fitted loss 0.13769800961017609 versus 0.13769799470901489 (+1.49e-08, relative 1.1e-07), and the reported optimum moves from c12 0.0985 nm to 0.0 nm and phi12 1.134 rad to -1.465 rad. The scientific conclusion is unchanged but the published numbers are not.

peak_allocated_bytes.note: Measured device.currentAllocatedSize after the fit. Each extra candidate adds one chi table (2097152 B), one cross table (73211904 B), one Nyquist table (65536 B) and two phase-sum planes (1048576 B each) = 77471744 B, so K=4 adds 309.9 MB to an 11.36 GB engine, 2.7%. The register/occupancy cost is not directly observable without Metal counters; what is observable is that the batched path is slower at every footprint.

ranked_bottlenecks_ms_per_evaluation: 155 ms - blocked intermediate write + read, 18.82 GB of the 28.2 GB device traffic. Not removable: see lever_a_intermediate.
78 ms - bright-field G read, 9.41 GB at the measured 121 GB/s streaming ceiling. Mandatory.
25.6 ms - both 512-point inverse transforms, already at peak float32 throughput. Measured by removing them at identical traffic.

~20 ms - row-pass efficiency gap: 120.1 ms for 13.9 GB (115.7 GB/s) against 138.8 GB/s for the column pass. The row pass enumerates only 128 threadgroups of 256 threads, so wave packing is a plausible cause, but splitting its bright-field range changes the float32 accumulation order of the phase sums and is therefore not trajectory-neutral.
1.5-1.7 ms - wall-minus-GPU time at low host load. This is CPU encode contention, not synchronization: it rises to 23-24 ms only when three agents share the host.

rejected_arms.aba: Balanced-order interleaved A/B at 8 planes per candidate: batched/sequential 1.120, 0.905, 0.898, 0.952, 0.910, 0.905; full fit 74.62-74.86 s against 67.99 s.

rejected_arms.reason: Monotonically worse, which refutes the residency explanation of the K=4 null result and shows the shared bright-field chunk is never served from cache. The 2-plane arm additionally breaks the bit-identical contract (maxabs 1.490e-08) because the per-dispatch plane count sets the register accumulation depth of the phase sums.

rejected_arms.arm: unified cache layout / single-command-buffer transpose (round 1, re-confirmed here)
rejected_arms.change: Make the redraw read the column-major layout so the 334-447 ms per-switch transpose disappears.
rejected_arms.measured: Redraw-pattern read bandwidth over the same 9.43 GB: 102.0 GB/s row-major against 13.6 GB/s column-major.
rejected_arms.reason: Rejected. Reading the loss's blocked layout from the redraw costs 0.693 s instead of 0.092 s, which is 600 ms of new redraw time against at most 335-447 ms of saved transpose. Also out of scope: the optimizer never alternates layouts, so a real fit pays the transpose at most once per workflow, not once per evaluation.

rejected_arms.change: Replace the blocked 4-row store with a linear store (ssb_correct_half_column_ifft512_hermitian_linear).
rejected_arms.measured: Column-only 155.3 ms against 157.7 ms for the blocked store, i.e. neutral.
rejected_arms.reason: The store pattern is not the limiter; the intermediate round trip is real device traffic at the machine's mixed-stream ceiling. Reverted.

rejected_arms.change: Remove the 512-point inverse transforms from both loss kernels at identical global traffic (timing only, parity intentionally broken).
rejected_arms.measured: gpu p50 224.9 and 222.4 ms against 250.5, 256.1 and 249.4 ms.
rejected_arms.reason: The entire transform work of both passes is worth 25.6 ms of a 250 ms evaluation and is already at peak float32 throughput, so there is no arithmetic headroom. Recorded as a bound, not a candidate.

results.what_would_be_needed: The evaluation is 295 ms against a hardware floor of roughly 235 ms made of 9.41 GB of mandatory bright-field reads plus 18.82 GB of intermediate traffic at the measured 121-139 GB/s. The only large win left would be an algorithm that does not need a 512x512 complex64 transpose buffer per bright-field term - for example folding the aberration-dependent correction into a form whose 2D transform is candidate-independent. The correction is not factorable that way: ssb_corrected_value_precomputed_chi multiplies each cached value by a unit complex number built from a per-candidate per-pixel chi table and a per-candidate per-bright-field per-coordinate cross table, so the transform input genuinely depends on the candidate at every pixel.

accumulate_first_variant.question: IFFT2 is linear, so could the per-bright-field corrected planes be summed in the q domain first and a single transform performed per candidate, removing the 18.82 GB intermediate round trip?
accumulate_first_variant.verdict: not available for this objective; the constraint is structural, not numerical
accumulate_first_variant.constraint: The per-pixel quantity is the variance of the phase ACROSS bright-field terms, so a phase has to exist per bright-field term. ssb_ifft512_rows_hermitian_phase_moments accumulates `float sum[8]`/`sumsq[8]` over local_bf through `phase = atan2(dc_spatial.y + h + delta.y, dc_spatial.x + delta.x)` and only then writes phase_sum[pixel] += sum[lane]; phaseVariance assembles sumOfSquares/(logical*pixels) - squareOfMeans/pixels, which is mean over pixels of (mean over bright field of phase^2 minus (mean over bright field of phase)^2). The nonlinearity sits between the transform and the sum, and the sum is over phases, not over complex amplitudes, so IFFT2 linearity has no sum to commute with.
accumulate_first_variant.second_barrier: The Nyquist boundary correction is added inside the atan2 argument and is indexed by the bright-field term: boundary_base = local_bf * 2n, delta = +/-nyquist_correction[boundary_base + col] +/- nyquist_correction[boundary_base + n + row]. It is not the transform of any accumulated spectrum, so even a complex-plane accumulator would still need a per-bright-field term inside the atan2.
accumulate_first_variant.already_implemented_elsewhere: The accumulate-first structure does exist in this engine, and is used exactly where the output IS linear: reconstruct() calls setCacheColumnMajor(false), clears `accumulator`, and runs ssb_gamma_accumulate_half(..., device float2 *accumulator [[buffer(15)]], ...) to sum the corrected bright-field planes into one 512x512 complex64 q-domain accumulator before a single transform. It reads the same 9.41 GB of G in 71-84 ms, i.e. 120-132 GB/s, which is the measured G-read floor. That is the structure the loss cannot use.
accumulate_first_variant.price_if_the_user_redefines_the_objectiv: Device traffic would fall from 28.2 GB to about 9.4 GB per evaluation, removing roughly 155 ms of the 295 ms evaluation and taking the fit from 61.97 s to roughly 30 s. It is not a float32-epsilon change: the current per-pixel quantity is a sum of 8937 phases, whereas the variant's per-pixel quantity is a single angle in [-pi, pi], so the loss would move by O(1), not O(1e-7). Landing it would be a different objective that needs its own scientific validation and a recaptured frozen gate, so it is recorded as a decision for the user and was not built.

arm_inventory_audit.purpose: Confirm no measurement arm silently failed and was dropped from the tables.
arm_inventory_audit.aborted_launches: Two launch attempts produced no data and no arm: an initial background launch (2 s) and one using setsid, which does not exist on macOS ('command not found: setsid'). Both predate the successful run and only mean a retry, not a dropped arm.
arm_inventory_audit.deliberately_killed: A queued probe4 job (k4b) was killed while waiting behind three other agents and replaced by an equivalent run (k4c) with the same inputs; k4c completed all three footprint arms.
arm_inventory_audit.superseded: The first K=4 probe (metal-runs/lowload/k4, 3 rounds, unbalanced arm order, host load 2.95) gives speedups 1.127, 0.752, 1.015, 0.906, 0.974, 0.996 with 0 bit mismatches, median 0.94x. It agrees with the balanced ppc=8 arm (0.908x) and is superseded by it because the arm order was not counterbalanced.

intermediate_pass_count.proposed_target: Reduce the blocked intermediate round trip from 4 passes to 2 with a four-step / two-stage 512x512 decomposition, for a predicted ~38% cut in fit wall time (61.97 s -> high 30s).
intermediate_pass_count.verdict: not achievable, and the target does not exist: the loss intermediate is already written once and read once, i.e. exactly 2 passes. No GPU time was spent because the premise fails on inspection and the measurement that distinguishes a 2-pass from a 4-pass model already exists.
intermediate_pass_count.where_the_2_10_MB_figure_comes_from: Swift `plane = size * size` = 262144 elements = 2097152 B for complex64. That is the full-plane allocation unit, and it sizes accumulator, finalTemporary, fftA (32 planes = 67.1 MB) and the two phase-sum buffers. It is NOT the loss intermediate's per-bright-field traffic. The intermediate is halfPlane = size * (size / 2 + 1) = 512 * 257 = 131584 elements = 1052672 B, which is the stride the Swift side passes as `halfBytes` for the bright-field cache and which the kernel uses as `constexpr uint plane = n * half_cols`.
intermediate_pass_count.code_level_count: The column pass stores exactly 64 threads * 8 slots * 257 columns = 131584 float2 per bright-field term, each element once, and the row pass loads exactly 1028 float2 * 128 row blocks = 131584 float2 per term, each element once. There is no separate transpose kernel in the loss path: the column pass writes directly into the transposed blocked-4-row layout and the row pass reads that layout directly, so the transpose is fused into the two passes.

measured_traffic_and_closure.conclusion: The 2-pass model predicts 28.23 GB at the observed 105.7 GB/s aggregate, i.e. 266 ms against 267.1 ms measured. A 4-pass round trip would need at least 9.41 + 4*9.41 = 47.0 GB, i.e. 339 ms at the column pass's demonstrated 138.8 GB/s and 406 ms at the row pass's 115.7 GB/s. The measurement sits 27-36% below the 4-pass floor, far outside the +-10% host-load sensitivity, so it excludes the 4-pass model.

per_pass_checks.column_pass: 9.41 GB read + 9.41 GB write in 135.6 ms = 138.8 GB/s
per_pass_checks.row_pass: 9.41 GB read + 4.69 GB L2-resident read-modify-write in 120.1 ms = 115.7 GB/s

intermediate_pass_count.why_no_factorization_beats_two_passes: The axis separation IS the transpose: stage 1 transforms the 512-element row axis from a contiguous 4 KB column, and stage 2 needs all 257 columns for every output row. The intermediate's size is invariant under the transform, so a four-step, six-step or tiled factorization all still materialise a full 1052672 B plane between their stages, and tiling it into the 32768 B threadgroup budget adds passes rather than removing them. The only way to reach zero passes is to hold the plane on chip, which the threadgroup budget refutes.
intermediate_pass_count.residual_headroom: The row pass runs at 115.7 GB/s against the column pass's 138.8 GB/s, worth about 20 ms per evaluation, roughly 4 s of a 62 s fit (~7%). It is not trajectory-neutral to attack: splitting the row pass's bright-field range across more threadgroups changes the float32 accumulation order of the phase sums, which this experiment measured to matter at the 1.49e-08 level.

outputs.result: Pristine 597b566 (exact frozen source) fit at 8937 BF: 61.97 s = 54.18 s of 201 global-trial evaluations plus 7.19 s of 27 Nelder-Mead refinements at host load 1.86; fitted loss 0.13769799470901489, bit-identical to the frozen reference 0.1376979947090149. This is the headline before/after number: unchanged.

Unbatched control arm of the A/B (identical source path, temporary evaluateBatch wiring compiled in but not enabled): 67.99 s = 59.29 s trials + 8.01 s refinement at host load 3.28, fitted loss 0.13769799470901489. The 6.0 s spread against the 61.97 s quiet run is host load, not a code difference.

Batched arm K=2 via evaluateBatch: 74.86 s = 66.21 s trials + 8.04 s refinement at host load 3.28, i.e. 0.908x (10% slower). Fitted loss 0.13769800961017609, +1.49e-08 versus the control. Only 11 of 200 trial points are shared with the control; the TPE trajectory diverges at trial index 11.

Batched arm K=4 via evaluateBatch: 74.62 s = 65.92 s trials + 8.08 s refinement at host load 3.28, i.e. 0.911x (9% slower). Fitted loss 0.13769800961017609, +1.49e-08 versus the control; only 10 of 200 trial points are shared, divergence at trial index 10. All 200 trial points re-evaluated through the single-candidate path give max absolute deviation 0.000e+00, max relative deviation 0.000e+00 and 0 bit mismatches, so the objective itself is exact and the loss difference is purely a search-trajectory effect.

Multi-candidate objective at the default 8-plane per-candidate chunk, 3 balanced-order rounds of 2 groups of 4 candidates: batched/sequential 1.120, 0.905, 0.898, 0.952, 0.910, 0.905 (median 0.908x). Per-candidate losses bit-identical (maxabs 0.000e+00) in all six comparisons. Host load 0.70.

Same arm with a 4-plane per-candidate chunk so the shared bright-field read is at most 4.2 MB: 0.961, 0.775, 0.772, 0.797, 0.771, 0.768 (median 0.773x). Halving the footprint makes batching worse, refuting the L2-residency explanation of the K=4 null result.

Same arm with a 2-plane per-candidate chunk: 0.666, 0.554, 0.527, 0.528, 0.561, 0.528 (median 0.541x). Dispatch overhead dominates; also breaks the bit-identical contract (maxabs 1.490e-08 on the group-0 comparisons), because the per-dispatch plane count sets the register accumulation depth of the phase sums.

Device limits measured on the M5: maxThreadgroupMemoryLength 32768 bytes, recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize 19.07 GB. L2-resident read peaks at 2957 GB/s at a 24 MB working set and has collapsed to 159 GB/s by 256 MB. The blocked 4-row store pattern (32 bytes per 8224-byte stride, the column pass's output layout) measures 73 GB/s at an 8.4 MB working set - the worst pattern in the suite. Redraw-pattern reads measure 102 GB/s row-major versus 13.6 GB/s column-major over the same 9.43 GB.

Loss-only pass ablation with the round-1 SSB_PROFILE_SKIP_* gates at host load 2.3: full loss gpu p50 267.1 ms; column-only 135.6 ms, row-only 120.1 ms, nyquist-only 9.4 ms, additive 265.1 ms. Every pass is separately throughput-limited and they do not overlap.

Timing-only arm with both 512-point inverse transforms removed from the two loss kernels at identical global traffic (parity intentionally broken): gpu p50 224.9 and 222.4 ms against 250.5, 256.1 and 249.4 ms for the full kernels. The complete FFT arithmetic of both passes is worth only ~11%, so the objective is not FFT-bound.
Column-pass-only variant of the same arm: 241.1 and 246.9 ms, i.e. the 512-point transform inside the column pass costs ~9 ms of the 250 ms evaluation.
Row-pass-only variant: gpu p50 230.8 ms, so the row pass's transform costs ~20 ms. The two transforms are additive and together account for the 25.6 ms measured by the both-nofft arm.
